<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">INVESTORS FINANCIAL SERVICES CORP.<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)<br> Years Ended December 31, 2005, 2004 and 2003</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 15.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-15.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">10. Company Obligated Mandatorily Redeemable
Preferred Securities of Subsidiary Trust Holding Junior&#160; Subordinated Deferrable Interest Debentures of
the Company</font> (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Securities.
Therefore, the Company presents in its consolidated financial statements junior
subordinated debentures as a liability and its investment in ICTI as a
component of other assets. The income for the three months during 2003 that
ICTI was not consolidated is considered immaterial.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a11_StockholdersEquity_081013"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">11. Stockholders&#146; Equity</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2005, the Company&#146;s capital
stock consisted of authorized 1,000,000 shares of preferred stock and
175,000,000 shares of common stock, all with a par value of $0.01 per share.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At the Annual Meeting of Stockholders of the Company
held on April&nbsp;13, 2004, stockholders approved an increase in the number of
authorized shares of common stock from 100,000,000 to 175,000,000. On May&nbsp;5<font style="letter-spacing:-.1pt;">, 2004, the Company amended its Certificate of
Incorporation to increase the number of authorized shares of common stock to
175,000,000. These shares are available for issuance for general corporate
purposes as determined by the Company&#146;s Board of Directors.</font></font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has four equity incentive plans: the
Amended and Restated 1995 Stock Plan (&#147;Stock Plan&#148;), the Amended and Restated
1995 Non-Employee Director Stock Option Plan (&#147;Director Plan&#148;), the 1997
Employee Stock Purchase Plan (&#147;ESPP&#148;) and the 2005 Equity Incentive Plan, which
was approved by the stockholders on April&nbsp;14, 2005 (the &#147;2005 Plan&#148;). The
2005 Plan supersedes both the Stock Plan and the Director Plan, both of which
continue in effect only with regard to options outstanding under those plans. Pursuant
to the terms of the 2005 Plan, awards under the 2005 Plan may include incentive
stock options, nonstatutory stock options, stock appreciation rights,
restricted stock, restricted stock units and performance units, qualified
performance-based awards, and stock grants. There were no amendments to any
plans during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Effective with the start of the 2005 Plan, 45,703
shares of the Director Plan and 3,439,197 shares of the Stock Plan were
transferred to the 2005 Plan. On April&nbsp;14, 2005, the shareholders
authorized an additional 2,000,000 shares of common stock for issuance under
the 2005 Plan.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Of the shares authorized for issuance under the 2005
Plan at December&nbsp;31, 2005, 4,104,013 were available for grant as of that
date. No options were granted to consultants during the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2005, 2004 and 2003.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At the Annual Meeting of Stockholders of the Company
held on April&nbsp;13, 2004, stockholders approved an amendment to the Company&#146;s
ESPP to increase the number of shares of common stock that may be issued
thereunder from 1,120,000 to 1,620,000.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has recorded deferred compensation of $0.3
million and $0.6 million at December&nbsp;31, 2005 and 2004, respectively. Amortization
of deferred compensation was $0.3 million, $0.3 million and $0.5&nbsp;million
for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2005, 2004 and 2003, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under the terms of the ESPP, the Company may issue up
to 1,620,000 shares of common stock pursuant to the exercise of nontransferable
options granted to participating employees. The ESPP permits eligible employees
to purchase up to 8,000 shares of common stock per payment period, subject to
limitations provided by Section&nbsp;423(b)&nbsp;of the Internal Revenue Code,
through accumulated payroll deductions. The purchases are made twice a year at
a price equal to the lesser of (i)&nbsp;90% of the market value of the common
stock on the first business day of the payment period (rounded to the next
quarter-dollar), or (ii)&nbsp;90% of the market value of the common stock on
the last business day of the payment </font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2004, the

of the common stock on the first business day of the payment periods ending June&nbsp;30,
2003 and December&nbsp;31, 2003, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In July&nbsp;2005, the Company announced that its
Board of Directors authorized a repurchase plan of up to $150.0&nbsp;million of
the Company&#146;s common stock in the open market over the twelve months following
the announcement. The plan expires in June&nbsp;2006. During the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2005, the Company repurchased $70.7 million of its common stock.</font></p>

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">INVESTORS FINANCIAL SERVICES CORP.<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)<br> Years Ended December 31, 2005, 2004 and 2003</font></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">12. Comprehensive Income</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Comprehensive
income represents the change in equity of the Company during a period from
transactions and other events and circumstances from non-shareholder sources. It
includes all changes in equity during a period except those resulting from
investments by shareholders and distributions to shareholders. The Company&#146;s
other comprehensive income and related tax effects for the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2005, 2004 and 2003 are as follows (Dollars in thousands):</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">INVESTORS FINANCIAL SERVICES CORP.<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)<br> Years Ended December 31, 2005, 2004 and 2003</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a13_EmployeeBenefitPlans_081337"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">13. Employee Benefit Plans</font></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pension Plan</font></i></b></font><b><i><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">&#151;</font></i></b>The Company has a trusteed,
noncontributory, qualified defined benefit pension plan (&#145;Pension Plan&#146;)
covering substantially all of its employees who were hired before January&nbsp;1,
1997. The benefits are based on years of service and the employee&#146;s
compensation during employment. Generally, the Company&#146;s funding policy is to
contribute annually the maximum amount that can be deducted for federal income
tax purposes. Contributions are intended to provide not only for benefits
attributed to &#160;service to date, but also
for benefits expected to be earned in the future. The plan document was amended
in December&nbsp;2001 and December&nbsp;2004 to freeze benefit accruals for
certain highly compensated participants. Effective January&nbsp;1, 2006, no
further Pension Plan benefit will accrue on behalf of any Pension Plan
participant, and effective December&nbsp;31, 2005, all Pension Plan participant&#146;s
accounts were frozen. The Company uses a December&nbsp;31 measurement date for
this plan.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Supplemental
Retirement Plan</font></i></b></font><b><i><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">&#151;</font></i></b>The
Company also has a nonqualified, unfunded, supplemental retirement plan (&#145;SERP&#146;)
which was established in 1994 and covers certain employees and pays benefits
that supplement any benefits paid under the Pension Plan. Benefits under the
SERP are generally based on compensation not includable in the calculation of
benefits to be paid under the Pension Plan. The plan document was amended in April&nbsp;2000
to eliminate the compensation cap and include bonuses and commissions of
certain employees. The Company uses a December&nbsp;31 measurement date for
this plan.</p>

following table sets forth the status of the Company&#146;s Pension Plan and SERP
(Dollars in thousands):</font></p>

and $14.0 million at December&nbsp;31, 2005 and 2004, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s core
investment objectives for the Pension Plan are long-term capital appreciation and
growth of income, while protecting the principal value of trust assets from
long-term permanent loss and, within reason, from large short-term fluctuations.
The approved investment policies of the trust anticipate fixed income
investments to compose 25-55% and equity securities to compose 45-75%
of the total portfolio. Cash equivalents may be used to provide liquidity,
income and stability to the portfolio.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cash and short-term
investments represent money market funds at December&nbsp;31, 2005 and 2004. Equity
securities supply current income and growth through market appreciation. The
Company invests in quality companies with securities that are readily
marketable. The equity securities portfolio is diversified with no more than
10% of the portfolio invested in any one particular industry at December&nbsp;31,
2005 and 2004. Debt securities offer a source of current income and reduce the
variability of the portfolio&#146;s total market value. Fixed income investments
were limited to issues by the United States Government and its agencies, and
investment grade corporate bonds at December&nbsp;31, 2005 and 2004. The
Pension Plan was in full compliance with the approved pension objectives and
policies for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2005 and 2004. At December&nbsp;31,
2005 and 2004, the pension did not hold any securities of the Company.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company does not
expect to contribute to its Pension Plan during 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2005
and 2004, the SERP remained an unfunded plan. The Company does not expect to
contribute to the SERP during 2006.</font></p>

years (Dollars in thousands):</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 10.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Employee Savings Plan</font></i></b></font><b><i><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">&#151;</font></i></b>The Company sponsors a qualified
defined contribution employee savings plan covering substantially all employees.
The Company matches employee contributions to the plan up to specified amounts.
The total cost of this plan to the Company was $3.7 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2005 and $3.2 million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2004 and 2003.</p>

 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">INVESTORS FINANCIAL SERVICES CORP.<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)<br> Years Ended December 31, 2005, 2004 and 2003</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a14_OffBalanceSheetFinancialInstr_081340"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">14. Off
Balance Sheet Financial Instruments</font></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Lines of Credit</font></i></b></font><b><i><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">&#151;</font></i></b>At December&nbsp;31, 2005, the
Company had commitments to mutual funds and individuals under collateralized
open lines of credit totaling $1.1 billion, against which $240.3&nbsp;million
in loans were drawn. The credit risk involved in issuing lines of credit is
essentially the same as that involved in extending demand loans. The Company
does not anticipate any loss as a result of these lines of credit.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Securities Lending</font></i></b></font><b><i><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">&#151;</font></i></b>On behalf of its clients, the
Company lends securities to creditworthy broker-dealers. In certain
circumstances, the Company may indemnify its clients for the fair market value
of those securities against a failure of the borrower to return such securities.
The Company requires the borrowers to provide collateral in an amount equal to,
or in excess of, 102% of the fair market value of U.S. dollar-denominated
securities borrowed and 105% of the fair market value of non-U.S.
dollar-denominated securities borrowed. The borrowed securities are revalued
daily to determine whether additional collateral is necessary. As guarantor,
the Company is required to recognize, at the inception of a guarantee, a
liability for the fair value of the obligation undertaken in issuing the
guarantee. The Company measures the fair value of its indemnification
obligation by marking its securities lending portfolio to market on a daily
basis and comparing the value of the portfolio to the collateral holdings
position. The fair value of the indemnification obligation to be recorded would
be the deficiency of collateral as compared to the value of the securities out
on loan.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">With respect to the
indemnified securities lending portfolio, the cash and U.S. government
securities held by the Company as collateral at December&nbsp;31, 2005 totaled
$7.7 billion, while the fair value of the portfolio totaled approximately
$7.4&nbsp;billion. Given that the collateral held was in excess of the value of
the securities that the Company would be required to replace if the borrower
defaulted and failed to return such securities, the Company&#146;s indemnification
obligation was zero and no liability was recorded.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All securities loans are
categorized as overnight loans. The maximum potential amount of future payments
that the Company could be required to make would be equal to the market value
of the securities borrowed. Since the securities loans are overcollateralized
by 2% (for U.S. dollar- denominated securities) to 5% (for non-U.S.
dollar-denominated securities) of the fair market value of the loan made, the
collateral held by the Company would be used to satisfy the obligation. In
addition, each borrowing agreement includes &#147;set-off&#148; language that allows the
Company to use any excess collateral on other loans to that borrower to cover
any collateral shortfall of that borrower. However, there is a potential risk
that the collateral would not be sufficient to cover such an obligation if the
security on loan increased in value between the time the borrower defaulted and
the time the security is &#147;bought-in.&#148;&#160; In
those instances, the Company would &#147;buy-in&#148; the security using all available
collateral and a loss would result from the difference between the value of the
security &#147;bought-in&#148; and the value of the collateral held. The Company has
never experienced a broker default.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a15_DerivativeFinancialInstrument_081341"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">15. Derivative
Financial Instruments</font></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 2.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest Rate Contracts</font></i></b></font><b><i><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">&#151;</font></i></b>Interest rate contracts involve an
agreement with a counterparty to exchange cash flows based on an underlying
interest rate index. A swap agreement involves the exchange of a series of
interest payments, either at a fixed or variable-rate, based upon the notional
amount without the exchange of the underlying principal amount. The Company&#146;s
exposure from these interest rate contracts results from the possibility that
one party may default on its contractual obligation when the contracts are in a
gain position. The Company has experienced no terminations by counterparties of
interest rate swaps. Credit risk is limited to the positive fair value of the
derivative financial instrument, which is significantly </p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">32</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-32',FILE='C:\JMS\dperry\06-2415-1\task869015\2415-1-fs.htm',USER='dperry',CD='Mar  2 09:43 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">INVESTORS FINANCIAL SERVICES CORP.<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)<br> Years Ended December 31, 2005, 2004 and 2003</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">15.
Derivative Financial Instruments</font> (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 2.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">less than the
notional value. As of December&nbsp;31, 2005, the positive fair value related
to the Company&#146;s interest rate contracts was approximately $24.3 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 2.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company enters into
pay-fixed/receive-floating interest rate swap agreements. These instruments
have been designated as cash flow hedges of variable-rate liabilities and a
forecasted series of fixed-rate overnight liabilities incurred at different
daily fixed rates (thereby resulting in a variable interest expense pattern). The
contractual or notional amounts of the interest rate swap agreements held by
the Company were approximately $1.9 billion and $1.6 billion at December&nbsp;31,
2005 and 2004, respectively. These contracts had net fair values of
approximately $24.2 million and $1.5 million at December&nbsp;31, 2005 and
2004, respectively. These fair values are included in the respective other
assets and other liabilities categories on the Company&#146;s consolidated balance
sheets. See also Note 17 for additional information on the fair value of the
interest rate contracts.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 2.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2005 and 2004, the Company recognized net pre-tax gains of $3.5 million and
$4.1 million, respectively, which represented the total ineffectiveness for all
cash flow hedges. For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2003, total
ineffectiveness related to cash flow hedges had an insignificant impact on
earnings.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2005, the Company expects that
approximately $9.3 million of deferred net after-tax gains on derivative
contracts included in other comprehensive income will be reclassified to net
interest income within the next twelve months. This expectation is based on the
net discounted cash flows from existing cash flow hedging derivatives, as well
as the amortization of gains from the terminated cash flow hedging derivatives.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Foreign Exchange
Contracts&#151;</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">Foreign </font></i></b></font>exchange
contracts involve an agreement to exchange the currency of one country for the
currency of another country at an agreed-upon rate and settlement date. Foreign
exchange contracts consist of spot, forward and swap contracts. Spot contracts
call for the exchange of one currency for another and usually settle in two
business days. Forward contracts call for the exchange of one currency for
another at a date beyond spot. In a currency swap, the holder of a currency
transacts simultaneously both a spot and a forward transaction in that currency
for an equivalent amount of another currency to get temporary liquidity in the
currency owned. The Company&#146;s risk from foreign exchange contracts results from
the possibility that one party may default on its contractual obligation or
from movements in exchange rates. Credit risk is limited to the positive market
value of the derivative financial instrument, which is significantly less than
the notional value. The notional value of the Company&#146;s foreign exchange
contracts at December&nbsp;31, 2005 and 2004 was $6.3 billion and $6.9 billion,
respectively. As of December&nbsp;31, 2005, the Euro foreign exchange contracts
represented approximately 57% of the of the notional value outstanding. As of December&nbsp;31,
2004, the British Pound foreign exchange contracts represented approximately
43% of the notional value outstanding. Unrealized gains or losses resulting
from purchases and sales of foreign exchange contracts are included within the
respective other assets and other liabilities categories on the Company&#146;s
consolidated balance sheets. Unrealized gains in other assets were $20.8
million and $99.6 million at December&nbsp;31, 2005 and 2004, respectively. Unrealized
losses in other liabilities were $19.7 million and $98.5 million at December&nbsp;31,
2005 and 2004, respectively. See also Note 17 for additional information on the
fair value of the Company&#146;s foreign exchange contracts. Foreign exchange
contracts with the same counterparty are netted in the Company&#146;s consolidated
balance sheets when a master netting agreement exists. These contracts have not
been designated as hedging instruments; therefore, all changes in fair value
are included in asset servicing fees.</p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a15_DerivativeFinancialInstrument_091232"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">15. Derivative Financial Instruments (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;</font></i></b></font>The Company also enters into fixed price purchase
contracts that are designed to hedge the variability of the consideration to be
paid for the purchase of investment securities. By entering into these contracts,
the Company is fixing the price to be paid at a future date for certain
investment securities. At December&nbsp;31, 2005 and 2004, the Company had
$97.5 million and $672.2 million, respectively, of fixed price purchase
contracts outstanding to purchase investment securities. Changes in fair value
of these cash flow hedges are included as a component of other comprehensive
income.</p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a16_CommitmentsAndContingencies_085417"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">16. Commitments and Contingencies</font></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Restrictions on
Cash Balances</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;</font></i></b></font>The Company
is required to maintain certain average cash reserve balances. The average
required reserve balance with the Federal Reserve Bank (&#145;FRB&#146;) for the two-week
period including December&nbsp;31, 2005 was approximately $51.9 million. In
addition, the Company&#146;s balance sheet includes deposits totaling $43.9 million,
which were pledged to secure clearings with depository institutions at December&nbsp;31,
2005.</p>

conducts regular reviews of its fiduciary responsibilities and considers the
results in preparing its consolidated financial statements. In the opinion of
management, there were no contingent liabilities at December&nbsp;31, 2005 that
were material to the consolidated financial position or results of operations
of the Company.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On June&nbsp;27, 2003, the Company and an individual
employee of the Company were named in a lawsuit alleging, among other things,
that the Company breached an implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing in
a subadvisory contract with Opus Investment Management,&nbsp;Inc. (&#145;Opus&#146;), and
that the individual employee of the Company engaged in a breach of fiduciary
duties and tortious interference with a contract. Opus had been a subadviser to
the Merrimac Funds, for which the Company acts as investment adviser. Upon the
expiration of Opus&#146;s contract on June&nbsp;1, 2003, the Merrimac Funds elected
not to re-appoint Opus as subadviser. The lawsuit was filed in Superior Court
in Worcester, Massachusetts and seeks unspecified damages. The lawsuit is
currently in the discovery phase. The Company believes that the claims are
without merit and intends to vigorously defend the rights of the Company. However,
the Company cannot predict the outcome of this lawsuit at this time, and the
Company can give no assurance that it will not affect the Company&#146;s financial
condition or results of operations in a materially adverse way.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In July&nbsp;2000, two of the Company&#146;s Dublin
subsidiaries, Investors Trust&nbsp;&amp; Custodial Services (Ireland)&nbsp;Ltd.
(&#145;ITC&#146;) and Investors Fund Services (Ireland)&nbsp;Ltd. (&#145;IFS&#146;), received a
plenary summons in the High Court, Dublin, Ireland. The summons named ITC and
IFS as defendants in an action brought by the FTF ForexConcept Fund Plc (the &#145;Fund&#146;),
a former client. The summons also named as defendants FTF Forex Trading and
Finance, S.A., the Fund&#146;s investment manager, Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young, LLP, the
Fund&#146;s auditors, and Dresdner Bank-Kleinwort Benson (Suisse) S.A., a trading
counterparty to the Fund. The Fund is an investment vehicle organized in Dublin
to invest in foreign exchange contracts. A total of approximately
$4.7&nbsp;million had been invested in the Fund. Most of that money was lost
prior to the Fund&#146;s closing to subscriptions in June&nbsp;1999.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In January&nbsp;2001, ITC, IFS and the other
defendants named in the plenary summons received a statement of claim by the
Fund seeking unspecified damages allegedly arising from breach of contract,
misrepresentation and breach of warranty, negligence and breach of duty of
care, and breach of fiduciary duty, among others. The Company has notified its
insurers and intends to defend this claim vigorously. Based on its
investigation through December&nbsp;31, 2005, the Company does not expect this
matter to have a material adverse effect on its business, financial condition
or results of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Investors Financial Services Corp. and five of its

2005 and August&nbsp;15, 2005 assert that the defendants violated Sections 10(b)&nbsp;and
20(a)&nbsp;of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 during the period October&nbsp;15,
2003 until July&nbsp;15, 2005. Among other things, the complaint filed on September&nbsp;30,
2005 asserts that the defendants violated Sections 10(b)&nbsp;and 20(a)&nbsp;of
the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 during the period </font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Investors Financial

of Massachusetts, Boston, Massachusetts. Among other things, the complaints
assert that the defendants are liable for breach of fiduciary duty, unjust
enrichment, abuse of control, mismanagement, misappropriation of information,

Exchange Act of 1934. The complaint filed on September&nbsp;22, 2005 also seeks
reimbursement under the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002. The allegations in the
complaints predominantly relate to: (1)&nbsp;the Company&#146;s October&nbsp;2004
restatement of its financial results, and (2)&nbsp;the Company&#146;s July&nbsp;2005
revision of public guidance regarding its future financial performance. The
complaints seek unspecified damages, attorneys&#146; fees, accountant and expert
fees, and costs. We strongly believe that the lawsuits lack merit and we intend
to defend against the claims vigorously. However, we cannot predict the outcome
of the lawsuits at this time, and we can give no assurance that they will not
materially adversely affect our financial condition or results of operations.</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">INVESTORS FINANCIAL SERVICES CORP.<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)<br> Years Ended December 31, 2005, 2004 and 2003</font></b></p>


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">17. Fair Value
of Financial Instruments</font> (Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The fair value estimates presented herein are based on
pertinent information available to management at December&nbsp;31, 2005 and
2004. Although management is not aware of any factors that would significantly
affect the estimated fair value amounts, such amounts have not been
significantly revalued for the purposes of these consolidated financial statements
since those dates and, therefore, current estimates of fair value may differ
significantly from the amounts presented herein.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company uses the following methods and assumptions
to determine the fair value of selected financial instruments:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Short-term
financial assets and liabilities</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;</font></i></b></font>For
financial instruments with a short or no stated maturity, prevailing market
rates and limited credit risk, carrying amounts approximate fair value. Those
financial instruments include cash and due from banks, loans and deposits.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Securities,
available for sale and held to maturity</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;</font></i></b></font>Fair values
were based on prices obtained from an independent nationally recognized pricing
service, or in the absence of such, prices were obtained directly from selected
broker-dealers.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Securities sold
under repurchase agreements and short-term and other borrowings</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;</font></i></b></font>Fair values
of the Company&#146;s long-term borrowings and long-term repurchase agreements were
based on quoted market prices, when available, and prevailing market rates for
borrowings of similar terms. Carrying amounts for short-term borrowings and
short-term repurchase agreements approximate fair value due to the short-term
nature of these instruments.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest rate
contracts</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;</font></i></b></font>Fair values
were based on the estimated amount that the Company would receive or pay to
terminate the swap agreements, taking into account the current interest rates
and the creditworthiness of the swap counterparties.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Foreign exchange contracts</font></i></b></font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"><b><i><font style="font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;">&#151;</font></i></b></font>Fair values
were based on quoted market prices of comparable instruments. Foreign exchange
contracts have been reduced by offsetting balances with the same counterparty
where a master netting agreement exists.</p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="a18_RegulatoryMatters_085419"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">18. Regulatory Matters</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company and the Bank are subject to various
regulatory capital requirements administered by the federal banking agencies. Failure
to meet minimum capital requirements can initiate certain mandatory and
possibly additional discretionary actions by regulators that, if undertaken,
could have a direct material effect on the Company&#146;s and the Bank&#146;s financial
statements. Under capital adequacy guidelines and the regulatory framework for
prompt corrective action, the Bank must meet specific capital guidelines that
involve quantitative measures of the Bank&#146;s assets, liabilities, and certain
off-balance sheet items as calculated under regulatory accounting practices. The
Company&#146;s and the Bank&#146;s capital amounts and classification are also subject to
qualitative judgments by the regulators about components, risk weightings, and
other factors.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Quantitative measures established by regulation to
ensure capital adequacy require the Company and the Bank to maintain minimum
amounts and ratios (set forth in the table below) of Total and Tier 1 capital
(as defined in the regulations) to risk-weighted assets (as defined), and of
Tier 1 capital (as defined) </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">37</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">to average assets (as

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2005, the most recent

<div>
 <p style="font-weight:bold;line-height:16.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 24.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">INVESTORS FINANCIAL SERVICES CORP.<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (Continued)<br> Years Ended December 31, 2005, 2004 and 2003.</font></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">18. Regulatory Matters
(Continued)</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Under Massachusetts law, trust companies such as the
Bank, like national banks, may pay dividends no more often than quarterly, and
only out of net profits and to the extent that such payments will not impair
the Bank&#146;s capital stock and surplus account. Moreover, prior Commissioner
approval is required if the total dividends for a calendar year would exceed
net profits for that year combined with retained net profits for the previous
two years. These restrictions on the ability of the Bank to pay dividends to
the Company may restrict the ability of the Company to pay dividends to its
stockholders.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The operations of the Company&#146;s securities broker
affiliate, Investors Securities Services, LLC (&#145;ISS&#146;), are subject to federal
and state securities laws, as well as the rules&nbsp;of both the SEC and the
NASD. Management believes, as of December&nbsp;31, 2005, that ISS is in
material compliance with all of the foregoing requirements to which it is
subject.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The operations of the Company&#146;s captive insurance
affiliate, Investors Vermont Insurance Company (&#145;IVIC&#146;), are subject to the
laws and regulations of the State of Vermont Department of Banking, Insurance,
Securities and Health Care Administration. Management believes, as of December&nbsp;31,
2005, that IVIC is in material compliance with all of the foregoing
requirements to which it is subject.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2004, the
Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (&#145;Basel Committee&#146;) released the
document &#147;International Convergence of Capital Measurement and Capital
Standards: A Revised Framework&#148;. The Framework, also referred to as Basel II,
is designed to secure international convergence on regulations and standards
governing the capital adequacy of internationally active banking organizations.
In September&nbsp;2005, the FFIEC (U.S. banking and thrift supervisory
agencies) revised guidance on the timing and qualification process for U.S.
banks that will become subject to Basel II. The new rules&nbsp;as applied in
the U.S. are expected to become effective on January&nbsp;1, 2009, subject to
transitional parallel testing beginning on January&nbsp;1, 2008. Although the
Company is not required to be compliant with the new rules, the Company is in the
process of developing an implementation program to achieve Basel II compliance.
Ultimately, U.S. implementation of Basel II will depend on, and will be subject
to, final regulations and related policies promulgated by the FFIEC supervisory
agencies. The Company cannot predict the final form of the rules, nor their
impact on the Company&#146;s risk-based capital.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Barclays Global Investors, N.A. (&#145;BGI&#146;) accounted for
18%, 17% and 16% of the Company&#146;s consolidated net operating revenues for the
years ended December&nbsp;31, 2005, 2004 and 2003, respectively. No client
other than BGI accounted for more than 10% of the Company&#146;s consolidated net
operating revenues in the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2005, 2004 and 2003.</font></p>
